channel.title: Nature Physics
channel.description: Nature Physics offers news and reviews alongside top-quality research papers in a monthly publication, covering the entire spectrum of physics. Physics addresses the properties and interactions of matter and energy, and plays a key role in the development of a broad range of technologies. To reflect this, Nature Physics covers all areas of pure and applied physics research. The journal focuses on core physics disciplines, but is also open to a broad range of topics whose central theme falls within the bounds of physics.

item.title: [7] Superconductivity on two surfaces
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Tingxin Li

Score 7/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Examines unusual superconducting states in multilayer graphene, a high-interest broad topic for the user.

Tags: #material #graphene #superconductivity

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03290-8 In rhombohedral multilayer graphene, superconductivity emerges from an unusual normal state in which electrons and holes reside on opposite surfaces of the crystal.

item.title: [8] Soft-X-ray momentum microscopy of nonlinear magnon interactions
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Bastian Pfau, Daniel Schick

Authors: Steffen Wittrock, Christopher Klose, Salvatore Perna, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Synchrotron-based momentum-resolved spectroscopy of collective excitations is highly relevant to an ARPES specialist.

Tags: #method #momentummicroscopy #magnons

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03318-z Short-wavelength magnons and their couplings are difficult to detect, limiting studies of nanoscale spin dynamics. Now a method using soft X-rays to image magnon momentum captures their nonlinear interactions with nanometre-scale sensitivity.

item.title: [8] Superconductivity from dual-surface carriers in rhombohedral graphene
item.content:encoded:
Last authors: Joshua Folk, Matthew Yankowitz

Authors: Manish Kumar, Derek Waleffe, Anna Okounkova, et al.

Score 8/10 B_IMPORTANT_CONDMAT

Why: Experimental evidence of electronic structure effects driving superconductivity in rhombohedral graphene.

Tags: #material #graphene #superconductivity

Abstract: Nature Physics, Published online: 05 June 2026; doi:10.1038/s41567-026-03277-5 Two different types of medium-thickness rhombohedral graphene are shown to exhibit multiple superconducting states. These states arise from wavefunctions that are localized mainly on their two outer layers.
